Need to search first.I couldn't write the Isaiah 43 notes this time, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

My first attempt to open the pages directly (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes) was refused. The tool will only open a page after a search has returned its link, and I hadn't searched yet. My follow-up searches didn't run either, because I had used up my tool allowance for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, I have nothing to cite. Notes written from memory would break both of those rules, so I've left them out rather than invent sources or URLs.

**Next time,** I'll search first and then read these, in this order:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Isaiah 43); Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on Bible Hub or StudyLight; Precept Austin's Isaiah 43 page.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** likely candidates are:
   - v. 3–4: Egypt given as a "ransom"
   - v. 7: "created for My glory" (Desiring God or Ligonier)
   - v. 25: God blotting out sins "for My own sake" (Spurgeon, Wesley's notes, Lutheran sources)
   - v. 27: who the "first father" is (Adam, Abraham or Jacob)
3. **Other views:** NET Bible translator notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship; Church Fathers on New Advent and Catholic Answers; any prosperity-teaching use of v. 2 and v. 19 ("I am about to do something new"), described only as those sites describe it.

If you send the request again, I'll begin with the searches so the pages can be opened and every point has a URL.
